answer: Each bid for an opal lot or pigment batch requires a compute ticket bound to its trading haven ID, lot ID, bidder key and an unpredictable daily seed. The verifier accepts a nonce only when SHA-256 of those fields plus the nonce has 24 leading zero bits, then records that ticket as spent. A fresh alias needs a different proof, averaging 2^24 hash trials per bid; new keys receive no free tickets. This prices bid flooding without proving unique operators, and GPU owners have an advantage.
